title: Encouraged by Thy Word
description: Encouraged by Thy Word in Tonic Solfa to DARWALL, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 81, “The beggar. Mt 7:7-8”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DARWALL; any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: En-cour-aged by thy word Of pro-mise to the poor; Be-hold, a beg-gar, Lord, Waits at thy mer-cy's door! No hand, no heart, O Lord, but thine, Can help or pi-ty wants like mine.

lines: No hand, no heart, O Lord, but thine,
Can help or pity wants like mine.
And pleas which move thy gracious ear,
Are such as men would scorn to hear.
I have no right to say
That though I now am poor,
Yet once there was a day
Thou know'st that from my very birth,
I've been the poorest wretch on earth.
My wants have been but few:
If thou shouldst leave my soul to starve,
It would be what I well deserve.
Thou often hast relieved my pain,
And often I must come again.
Though crumbs are much too good
For such a dog as I;
O do not frown and bid me go,
I must have all thou canst bestow.
I'll tell them of thy mercy's store,
And try to send a thousand more.
Such pleas as mine men would not bear,
But God receives a beggar's prayer.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to DARWALL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
